title: $E$-coefficient smooth base change
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, let $A=\mathcal O_E$ and fix a uniformizer $\varpi$. Consider a cartesian square [sbc-def-base-change-square]
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
Y&\xrightarrow{h}&X\\
e\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
T&\xrightarrow{g}&S.
\end{array}
$$
Assume that $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, all four schemes are noetherian, $X$ and $T$ have finite dimension, and $\ell$ is invertible on $S$. For each corner $W$, let $D_{\mathrm{comp}}(W,A)$ denote the full category of derived-complete complexes of modules over the completed coefficient sheaf $A_W$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], and define
$$D_{\mathrm{comp}}(W,E)=D_{\mathrm{comp}}(W,A)[1/\varpi]$$
by raw scalar localization [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. For $W=X,T$, use $\Dbc(W,E)=\Dbc(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)[1/\varpi]$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Rational completed pullback and direct image mean the scalar localizations of the corresponding integral completed functors [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]; their exchange is the scalar localization of the integral completed exchange.

Let $K_E\in\Dbc(T,E)$ admit a finite-level etale admissible lattice $L$ with a specified isomorphism $\iota:L[1/\varpi]\xrightarrow{\sim}K_E$ [sbc-def-admissible-lattices]. Then the exchange morphism is an isomorphism
$$
Lf^*_{\mathrm{comp},E}Rg_{*,\mathrm{comp},E}K_E
\xrightarrow{\sim}
Rh_{*,\mathrm{comp},E}Le^*_{\mathrm{comp},E}K_E
\quad\text{in }D_{\mathrm{comp}}(X,E).
$$
Its value at $K_E$, transported using $\iota$, is independent of the chosen admissible lattice and its presentation. If the lattice is square-constructibly admissible [sbc-def-admissible-lattices], this is an isomorphism in $\Dbc(X,E)$.

proof.text:
Check the coefficient hypotheses of the adic theorem. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $A$ is a DVR inside $E$, with finite residue field and nonzero uniformizer; by [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients], $A_n=A/(\varpi^{n+1})$ is finite. A PID is Noetherian: every ideal is generated by one element. Multiplication by $\varpi^{n+1}$ is injective in the domain $A$, so
$$0\longrightarrow A\xrightarrow{\varpi^{n+1}}A\longrightarrow A_n\longrightarrow0$$
is exact. Placing its first two terms in degrees $-1,0$ gives a bounded finite-free resolution, hence perfection by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Also $\ell=u\varpi^r$ for a unit $u$ and $r>0$, since $|\ell|_E=\ell^{-1}<1$ and the DVR decomposition applies. A power of $\ell$ thus annihilates $A_n$; its finite additive group has order a power of $\ell$: multiplication by $\varpi^j$ identifies each quotient $\varpi^jA/\varpi^{j+1}A$ with $A/\varpi A$ by cancellation in the domain. Since $\ell\in(\varpi)$, this finite residue field has characteristic $\ell$ and has $\ell^d$ elements for its finite dimension $d$ over $\mathbf F_\ell$. Counting the fibres in the quotient filtration gives $|A_n|=\ell^{d(n+1)}$. This order is invertible on $S$ and hence on every corner. The exponent $n+1$ here is the exponent $m$ in the positive-indexed coefficient datum.

source.place: Proof, opening two-term resolution; explicit arithmetic checks

proof.text: Choose $(L,\iota)$ from the hypothesis. By [sbc-def-admissible-lattices], $L\in\Dbc(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and each $L_n$ is in the essential image of $\Dbc(T_{\mathrm{et}},A_n)$. By [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], membership of $L$ includes derived completeness and compatible etale-origin witnesses for its reduction tower. Thus $L$ satisfies every input condition of [sbc-thm-adic-smooth-base-change]: the square and geometric hypotheses are exactly those of the statement, and step 1 supplies finiteness, invertible order, and perfection.

Apply [sbc-thm-adic-smooth-base-change] to $L$. With $F=P_fD_g$ and $G=D_hP_e$, it gives the specified integral completed exchange $\alpha_L:F(L)\xrightarrow{\sim}G(L)$. Its source and target are complete complexes on $X$: $D_g$ first lands on $S$, $P_f$ then on $X$; $P_e$ first lands on $Y$, $D_h$ then on $X$. The assertion concerns the ambient complete categories and does not require $D_g(L)$ to be bounded constructible.

source.place: Proof, integral lattice exchange from the adic theorem

proof.text: Use [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange] for the four arrows, and the Hom-module construction of [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. For each integral functor $H$ define $H_E$ on objects by $H$ and on tensors by $H_E(a\otimes c)=H(a)\otimes c$. This is balanced because $H(ra)=rH(a)$, and additive in both variables, so it is well defined on the tensor product. On pure tensors, preservation of composition is $H(ba)\otimes dc=H(b)H(a)\otimes dc$, and identities map to identities; by bilinearity these identities hold on all morphisms. The same formulas show that localization commutes with the composites $F,G$. No constructibility preservation of arbitrary direct images is being used.

source.place: Proof, central localization; functor construction on Hom modules

proof.text:
Write $Q_W$ for the localization functor on the complete category at corner $W$. For every complete integral object $M$ (not only admissible lattices), define $\alpha_{E,Q_TM}=Q_X(\alpha_M)$. The naturality identity in [lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange] tensor $c$ gives
$$G_E(a\otimes c)\,Q_X(\alpha_L)=Q_X(\alpha_{L'})\,F_E(a\otimes c).$$
Additivity proves naturality for every rational morphism, which is a finite sum of pure tensors. Thus these components form a transformation on the whole rationalized source. Its unit-square-counit formula is the integral formula with $Q$ applied: $Q$ preserves each composite, each inverse comparison, and the units and counits, whose triangle identities remain equalities. Therefore it is the specified rational exchange. From step 3, $Q_X(\alpha_L^{-1})$ is its inverse at the chosen lattice, since the two composites are $Q_X(1)=1$.

source.place: Proof, central localization of the specified exchange and its inverse

proof.text:
For any lattice presentation $i:Q_TL\xrightarrow{\sim}K_E$, the component on $K_E$ is
$$\beta_i=G_E(i)\,Q_X(\alpha_L)\,F_E(i)^{-1}.$$
For another presentation $i':Q_TL'\xrightarrow{\sim}K_E$, put $u=(i')^{-1}i$. The naturality proved in step 5 gives $Q_X(\alpha_{L'})F_E(u)=G_E(u)Q_X(\alpha_L)$. Substitute $i=i'u$ into the displayed expression and cancel $F_E(u)F_E(u)^{-1}$. The result is $\beta_i=G_E(i')Q_X(\alpha_{L'})F_E(i')^{-1}=\beta_{i'}$. This proves independence both of the lattice and of its specified identification with $K_E$. Notice that $u$ is a morphism in the raw rationalization [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]; no integral comparison of the lattices, common sublattice, or uniform bound on denominators on site objects is assumed.

source.place: Proof, independence of the admissible lattice; explicit conjugation identity

proof.text: Suppose $L$ is square-constructibly admissible. By [sbc-def-admissible-lattices], the four finite systems $D_{g,n}L_n$, $P_{f,n}D_{g,n}L_n$, $P_{e,n}L_n$, $D_{h,n}P_{e,n}L_n$ have constructible cohomology in one interval $[a,b]$. Put $H=D_gL$, $B=P_eL$, $J=P_fH$, and $J'=D_hB$. By [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] and [lemma-weil-pbc-completed-pullback-reduction], these four integral objects are complete, and their canonical reductions are respectively isomorphic to the four displayed finite systems. For $J$, first use the direct-image reduction of $H$ and then the pullback reduction; for $J'$, first use the pullback reduction of $B$ and then the direct-image reduction. All comparisons are natural and commute with quotient transitions. Hence the canonical reductions of $J,J'$ have constructible cohomology in $[a,b]$. If a direct-image comparison is read after restriction to $A_X$-modules, it still gives quotient-linear cohomology isomorphisms: [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] gives $A_X/I^nA_X=(P_n)_X$; locally lift $r$ in $(P_n)_X$ to $\widetilde r$ in $A_X$ and calculate $\phi(rx)=\phi(\widetilde r x)=\widetilde r\phi(x)=r\phi(x)$. Changing the lift has no effect because $I^n$ acts by zero. This proves the same intrinsic finite-coefficient constructibility and vanishing for the actual reductions. No conclusion with output category $S$ is used.

source.place: Proof, final four-system constructible landing sentence; canonical-reduction and compatible-witness expansion

proof.text:
For either $M=J$ or $M=J'$ on $X$, [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] supplies its canonical strict reduction tower and normalization isomorphisms $ho_{m,n}:M_m\otimes^L_{(P_m)_X}(P_n)_X\cong M_n$, inducing its transitions and satisfying the quotient cocycle. The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-normalized-constructible-local-effectivity] now hold: $X$ is Noetherian, the coefficient datum was checked in step 1, and the reductions have the common interval and intrinsic constructibility from step 7. That lemma supplies the uniform stratification and normalization-compatible local models required by [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-tower]. It also supplies bounded constructible etale origins $V_n$ with $c_n:
u_X^*V_n\cong M_n$. To obtain the compatible witnesses required by [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], use the coefficient-module comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and exactness of [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] to identify $
u_X^*(V_m\otimes^L_{P_m}P_n)$ with $(
u_X^*V_m)\otimes^L_{(P_m)_X}(P_n)_X$: on K-flat representatives the map sends $
u_X^{-1}(x\otimes r)$ to $
u_X^{-1}(x)\otimes r$. Here $P_n$ in the etale tensor denotes its constant coefficient sheaf, and both sides are complexes over $(P_n)_X$. Associativity follows from balancing. The isomorphism $c_n^{-1}ho_{m,n}(c_m\otimes^L(P_n)_X)$ then has source this inverse image and target $
u_X^*V_n$. Its etale source is bounded below: its inverse image is $M_n$, and the exact sheaf inverse image in [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level] reflects zero sheaves because its sheaf unit is an isomorphism. Thus cohomology vanishing is reflected as well. Full faithfulness on $D^+$ from [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] lifts this map and its inverse uniquely to $ eta_{m,n}:V_m\otimes^L_{P_m}P_n\cong V_n$. The defining equation is $c_n
u_X^*( eta_{m,n})=ho_{m,n}(c_m\otimes^L(P_n)_X)$. For $k\geq m\geq n$, substitute this equation twice: cancelling $c_m^{-1}c_m$ and using the cocycle for $ho$ makes the images of $ eta_{m,n}( eta_{k,m}\otimes^LP_n)$ and $ eta_{k,n}$ equal, under the canonical scalar-extension associativity identifications. Faithfulness gives the witness cocycle; the same calculation for $m=n$ gives the identity. Both objects therefore belong to $\Dbc(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ by its definition.

source.place: Proof, final four-system constructible landing sentence; canonical-reduction and compatible-witness expansion

proof.text: The category of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] is full. Since $J,J'$ lie in it by step 8, the integral exchange and its inverse from step 3 are both morphisms of this category. By [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], its raw rationalization is $\Dbc(X,E)$. Inclusion into the rationalized ambient complete category is fully faithful: the integral Hom groups on these endpoints are equal, hence their tensors with $E$ are equal. Therefore the localized exchange and its inverse of step 5 give an isomorphism in $\Dbc(X,E)$. For the specified presentation of $K_E$, represent its exchange by this constructible isomorphism through the endpoint identifications $F_E(i),G_E(i)$ in step 6. The equality proved there shows that the resulting exchange at $K_E$ is independent of the presentation. Here 'in $\Dbc(X,E)$' means this isomorphism under the fully faithful inclusion, with the indicated endpoint identifications; it does not infer integral constructibility of an arbitrary object solely from a rational isomorphism.

statement_change.what: STATEMENT-DISPUTED: both exchange endpoints are on X, not S. For S=T=Spec(k), X=Y=A1_k, g and h identities and f=e the structure map, the output is on A1_k. Correct S to X. Make the coefficient extension, completed A_W-module categories, raw Hom scalar localization and chosen lattice presentation explicit. Require finite dimension only for X and T, the domains of the existing Dbc definitions; do not instantiate Dbc at S or Y. Retain smooth f, qcqs g and the two distinct admissibility conditions.

citers.note: The input explicitly assumes the E-coefficient hypotheses at each finite stage, so finite dimensionality of X and T is inherited. Its displayed output is nevertheless D_comp(S, Qbar_ell), whereas both composites land on X. The citer requires its own output-category correction S to X. Its proof also claims coefficient-change compatibility not asserted by the E-coefficient theorem alone; that obligation must be audited in its own split.

old_proof.text:
The two-term free resolution
$[\mathcal O_E\xrightarrow{\varpi^{n+1}}\mathcal O_E]$ of $A_n$ and
the adic theorem [sbc-thm-adic-smooth-base-change] give the
statement for integral lattices; central localization (inverting
multiplication by $\varpi$) of
[def-weil-pbc-rational-category] gives
it for $K_E$, independent of the admissible lattice, and the
constructible landing is the four-system hypothesis of
[sbc-def-admissible-lattices].
